title: Predicting mixtures, identifying gains
subtitle: Meta Models · Limits of data curation · Reading LoRA
intro: Two main readings, two briefs, and three version watches recovered in the overlapping window: predicting experiments from training records and separating acceleration from persistent curation gains. The classic is LoRA and its factorized gradients.

blocks.text: The paper analyzes growing sample budgets in teacher–student perceptrons and distinguishes the effects empirically in LLMs. If the population training objective equals target loss and the baseline is globally optimal, reallocation cannot beat that optimum; finite-budget acceleration remains possible.[2]

articles.paper: Specialization, Diversity, and Scaling in Child-Scale Language Models
articles.authors: Steven Y. Feng · Michael C. Frank
articles.title: Sources and diversity at small data scale
articles.dateNote: First submitted 2026-10-27 · v1 · Recovered in the overlapping window

blocks.text: Based on the abstract: small GPT-2 models use BabyView home-recording transcripts and synthetic TinyDialogues, varying quantity, source, and diversity of child environments. Multiple children improve pooled held-out language prediction, without equally clear grammatical-benchmark gains; one loss does not represent every capability.[3]

articles.paper: Scaling and Renormalization in Neural Networks: An Effective Renormalization-Group Description of Grokking

articles.title: Effective critical exponents for grokking
articles.dateNote: First submitted 2026-10-26 · v1 · Recovered in the overlapping window

blocks.text: Based on the abstract: in two-layer modular-addition networks, a second-order loss expansion in per-neuron norms defines couplings, followed by Fiedler ordering and coarse-graining to estimate critical exponents. This concerns scaling of ML generalization transitions, rather than a universal model–data–compute budget power law.[4]

classic.question: At a fixed trainable-parameter budget, do gains come from the representable low-rank subspace or the optimization geometry induced by factorization?

blocks.text: Full fine-tuning stores all parameters per task; adapters (2019) add layers. Following low-intrinsic-dimension adaptation (2020), LoRA freezes pretrained weights and learns a low-rank increment that can be merged for deployment.[5,6]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Low-rank sufficiency is empirical and task-specific, not a theorem that full-tuning gradients remain low rank. The best rank depends on the metric in GPT-2 E2E experiments; transfer of fixed rank across models needs testing.[5]
